predecessors.name: Reformed Government of the Republic of China
predecessors.text: 'the RNG absorbed the Reformed Government (1938-1940)'; 'At formation, it controlled only Jiangsu, Anhui, and the north sector of Zhejiang'

predecessors.name: Provisional Government of the Republic of China
predecessors.text: 'the RNG absorbed ... the Provisional Government (1937-1940)'; kept 'semi-autonomous status as the North China Political Council'

successors.name: Republic of China
successors.text: 'After Japan's surrender in August 1945, the RNG dissolved'; its land returns to the Republic of China

ledger.x: 30 March 1940: 'On 30 March 1940, the RNG was established in Nanjing.'
ledger.cpn: Reformed Government of the Republic of China

ledger.x: 30 March 1940: 'The RNG absorbed the Reformed Government (1938-1940) and the Provisional Government (1937-1940)'; the former Provisional Government territory 'retained semi-autonomous status as the North China Political Council'; Shandong and Hebei were 'de jure part of this political entity' but 'under Japanese…
ledger.cpn: Provisional Government of the Republic of China

ledger.x: 24 March 1940: 'In 1940 an agreement was signed between the Inner Mongolian puppet state of Mengjiang and the RNG, incorporating the former into the latter as an autonomous part' (RNG page); the Mengjiang page gives the date 24 March 1940.
after 1940: 'The port of Shanghai and the cities of Hankou and Wuchang were also placed under control of the Reformed Government after 1940.'
December 1941: 'During the December 1941 Japanese offensive the Reorganized Government extended its control over Hunan, Hubei, and parts of Jiangxi provinces.'

9 January 1943: 'the RNG signed the Treaty on Returning Leased Territories and Repealing Extraterritoriality Rights with Japan, which abolished all foreign concessions within occupied China'; 'The RNG then took control of all of the international concessions in Shanghai and its other territories.'
19 August 1945: Mengjiang is disestablished (Mengjiang page, 'disestablished 19 August 1945'); the RNG page says only that the region 'remained only nominally under RNG authority'.
August 1945: 'After Japan's surrender in August 1945, the RNG dissolved.'

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: The regime fought no war of its own; it dissolved after Japan's surrender in August 1945.

certainty.note: The page gives the core provinces; the north was nominal (North China Political Council).

The page's wider claims (Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi in December 1941; Shanghai, Hankou, Wuchang 'after 1940') are undated or vague; the keyframe draws only the core, the nominal north and the Wuhan cities.
